nodes.text: You have the separate medicine cache from near the kiln. Will you bring it to the village?
We have the charter, the account, and the seal. There won't be a cleaner moment. Tell us what you are prepared to stand behind.
If you're looking for a lord, keep walking. If you're looking for work, we have more than we can afford.
The cart carried medicine. Take the coins from my desk if you must. Bring back the box.
Saint Orra once kept it open and held grain for lean seasons. Rookwatch took the toll after the abbey burned. Rusk calls every new demand an emergency.
The cart stopped on the south road. Medicine in a blue box. If the men around it are hungry, that doesn't make the box theirs.
Find the robbed cart east of Brackenford. The medicine is in its blue coffer. Return it to me; you need not kill the hungry men to recover it.
Find the robbed cart east of Brackenford. The medicine is in its blue coffer. Return it to me; you need not kill the hungry men to recover it.
You have the medicine. Will you hand it over now?
That's three fevers we can stop arguing with. Eighteen crowns, as promised.
Find a receipt. I can argue with a soldier. I need something I can put in front of a judge.
Read the levy notice and take the receipt from the checkpoint box at King's Trace. You owe the soldiers no payment. The woodland and eastern paths both pass around them.
Read the levy notice and take the receipt from the checkpoint box at King's Trace. You owe the soldiers no payment. The woodland and eastern paths both pass around them.
You have the notice and receipt. Shall we put the numbers on record?
Six taken, two declared. Even I can afford that arithmetic.
The ledger is here, and Wren has given terms. Shall we record your report?

choices.text: Here are the ledger and Wren's promise.

nodes.text: We will remember both the names and the promise.
The captain's seal is here. The valley must decide who keeps the road next. Will you stand before the writ table?

choices.text: Let us decide the road's future.

nodes.text: Discuss the resolution with me, then review the writ on the village table. Read all three outcomes before confirming one. You may leave the table without choosing.
Discuss the resolution with me, then review the writ on the village table. Read all three outcomes before confirming one. You may leave the table without choosing.
The writ is on the village table. Read all three resolutions before confirming one. You may leave the table without choosing.
This decides who receives the medicine. Delivering to the village permanently consumes the camp medicine and pays ten crowns. The other recipient receives none. This does not use the cart medicine.

choices.text: Deliver to the village for 10 crowns.

nodes.text: I'll tell them where it came from. They can decide what to forgive.
Wren says the fevers broke. The village still needs help, but I will not call those children less deserving.
At the village well, another list of names grew shorter. I'll tell them where it came from. They can decide what to forgive.
We voted for a road keeper. Astonishing how many people suddenly had opinions about ditches.
Ada has signed the levy in public. A seal is easier to trust when we can see whose hand holds it.
The toll bar is gone. We still have ditches to clear and travelers to shelter. Freedom has a long list of chores.

topics.text: What do you make of the road now?
What do you make of the road now?
What do you make of the road now?

nodes.text: A sword's just a promise with an edge. Yours has seen some difficult negotiations.
My hammer went missing at the kiln. Bring it back and I'll give you something worth sharpening.
My hammer is in a crate at the charcoal kiln west of King's Trace. Bring it to the forge; twelve crowns and an arming sword are yours.
My hammer is in a crate at the charcoal kiln west of King's Trace. Bring it to the forge; twelve crowns and an arming sword are yours.
You have brought what I asked for. Shall we settle the promise?

choices.text: I have what you asked for.

nodes.text: There. A blade that won't apologize on the first swing.
You've made enemies with better armor. Sensible time to visit a smith.

topics.text: What do you make of the road now?

nodes.text: Come in. There is stew on the fire and a roof overhead. Both have survived worse weather than this.
Blankets went to the ferry before the flood. My guests would like them back.
The blanket barrel is beside the stranded ferry southwest of the village. Bring them here for ten crowns and a permanently free bed.
The blanket barrel is beside the stranded ferry southwest of the village. Bring them here for ten crowns and a permanently free bed.
You have brought what I asked for. Shall we settle the promise?

choices.text: I have what you asked for.

nodes.text: A warm bed when you need one. Call it an investment in repeat business.
Four crowns for the bed. The roof's included, even where it leaks.
A warm bed when you need one. Your blankets have paid for it.
People have started paying old tabs. I may have to learn arithmetic.

topics.text: A bed for the night (4 crowns).
What do you make of the road now?

nodes.text: The charter survived below the chapel. The keepers still guard their order: reed, stone, flame. It was meant to teach mercy.
The bell has no rope. That is an observation, not an explanation.
Saint Orra promised shelter before judgment. Her successors preferred the reverse.
Reed for the traveler. Stone for the shelter. Flame for the watch. Offer them in that order: reed, stone, flame. A wrong note begins the sequence again.
The abbey kept a charter beneath the chapel. Its words survived the fire. Will you help me bring them back into daylight?
The crypt entrance stands below the split bell tower. Speak to me about the keepers, then read their clue and recover the charter. Bring it here for attestation.
The crypt entrance stands below the split bell tower. Speak to me about the keepers, then read their clue and recover the charter. Bring it here for attestation.
You have the charter and the keepers have yielded. Shall I attest what it says?
The words are plain. Keeping them will be harder.
Three candles remain among the monastery graves. Bring each one here. We can keep a small light for people who never came home.
Find three different candles around the monastery graves. Bring all three to this shelter for fifteen crowns and two bandages. We will light them here.
Find three different candles around the monastery graves. Bring all three to this shelter for fifteen crowns and two bandages. We will light them here.
You have brought what I asked for. Shall we settle the promise?

choices.text: I have what you asked for.

nodes.text: Three lights. A small answer to a large dark.
The crypt entrance stands beneath the split bell tower. Follow reed, stone, flame, recover the charter, and bring it here for attestation.
A charter cannot make people kind. It can make cruelty harder to call a duty.

topics.text: About A Bell Without a Rope.
Remind me: A Bell Without a Rope.
Finish A Bell Without a Rope.
What do you make of the road now?

nodes.text: The ferry hasn't moved in three weeks. Best safety record on the river.
My wife's ring is at the reed shrine. I left it there angry. I'd like not to leave it there forever.
Look in the offering bowl at Reed Shrine east of the village. Bring the ring to the ferry landing; eighteen crowns and a bandage are yours.
Look in the offering bowl at Reed Shrine east of the village. Bring the ring to the ferry landing; eighteen crowns and a bandage are yours.
You have brought what I asked for. Shall we settle the promise?

choices.text: I have what you asked for.

nodes.text: Thank you. That's all I've got that fits.
She'd have called all this a fuss. Then she'd have made you supper.

topics.text: Remind me: What the Reeds Keep.
What do you make of the road now?

nodes.text: You have the abbey's charter and the grain account. Shall I accept this evidence and open the storehouse?
An order bears a seal. An excuse usually borrows one.
Bring me the abbey's charter and the grain account. I will open a door. What you do beyond it is yours.
Present both documents to me. Beyond the storehouse lies Rusk's hall. Challenge him only when ready; his seal remains in the chest after victory. Bring that seal back to me.
Present both documents to me. Beyond the storehouse lies Rusk's hall. Challenge him only when ready; his seal remains in the chest after victory. Bring that seal back to me.
The captain is defeated and you carry his seal. Are you ready to report?

choices.text: Rusk is defeated. Here is his seal.

nodes.text: A captain is gone. A road still needs keeping. Take the seal to Mara.
My badge lies in a locker at the old watchtower. I left it there when I could no longer bear the orders it stood for.
The old watchtower locker holds my badge. Bring it to me in Rookwatch's courtyard for twenty crowns and a kite shield.
The old watchtower locker holds my badge. Bring it to me in Rookwatch's courtyard for twenty crowns and a kite shield.
You have brought what I asked for. Shall we settle the promise?

choices.text: I have what you asked for.

nodes.text: I thought I had lost the right to wear it.
This is enough. The storehouse door is open. Rusk has kept the seal below.
If we keep the road, we answer for everyone who walks it.
The village has named its keepers. My wardens will answer to the same public record.
My wardens have left the checkpoint. If someone needs protection, they will not have to buy it from a toll collector.

topics.text: Remind me: A Debt in Stone.
What do you make of the road now?

nodes.text: You have the separate medicine cache from near the kiln. Will you bring it to the camp?
I want my people alive when this is over.

choices.text: Testify, and I will argue for amnesty.
Testify, and repay what you took.

nodes.text: The account is in the old tower. Bring it here, and I'll put names to the numbers.

choices.text: I will bring you the ledger.

nodes.text: Some of us deserted a war. Some deserted a wage that never came. A few just liked the trees.
We took grain. Rusk took grain and called the receipt a law.
Rusk's grain account is in the old watchtower. I can tell you whose carts fill its pages. Will you hear our terms?
Find the ledger in the old watchtower, east of Rookwatch. Bring it to me, agree on testimony, then report our promise to Mara.
Find the ledger in the old watchtower, east of Rookwatch. Bring it to me, agree on testimony, then report our promise to Mara.
There are children under those tarps. They don't get a vote in what we call ourselves.

choices.text: I'll find medicine for the valley.

nodes.text: A separate medicine cache lies near the kiln, guarded by raiders. Take it to me or Mara. Either recipient pays ten crowns; only one receives it. The cart medicine belongs to another promise.
A separate medicine cache lies near the kiln, guarded by raiders. Take it to me or Mara. Either recipient pays ten crowns; only one receives it. The cart medicine belongs to another promise.
Bring me the watchtower ledger. Then we can agree on what my testimony will cost.
You will argue for amnesty in exchange for Wren's testimony. This promise is permanent. Both terms preserve the same access and thirty-crown report reward.
We'll put our names on it. That makes running harder.
You will require repayment in exchange for Wren's testimony. This promise is permanent. Both terms preserve the same access and thirty-crown report reward.
The first cart goes back tomorrow. Empty hands this time.
This decides who receives the medicine. Delivering to the camp permanently consumes the camp medicine and pays ten crowns. The other recipient receives none. This does not use the cart medicine.

choices.text: Deliver to the camp for 10 crowns.

nodes.text: There are children under those tarps. They don't get a vote in what we call ourselves.
Under the tarps, the fevers broke. Whatever else is written about us, let that be written too.
Mara received the medicine. I won't pretend my people did not need it. Our other promises still stand.
The road has changed. Our names and our promises remain. There is work enough to prove what either is worth.

nodes.text: You see stolen bread. I see a garrison that stayed when the crown stopped paying.
You see stolen bread. I see a garrison that stayed when the crown stopped paying.
Show that paper to the hungry and see whether they can eat it.
